headline: Supplier evaluation: LedgerBridge e-invoicing for Singapore, Australia, India — volume template next

suggested_routes.label: Internal / product / vendor note
suggested_routes.rationale: SpendNest is evaluating a supplier (LedgerBridge) for compliant e-invoicing; the next step is an internal data task.
suggested_routes.output: Vendor-evaluation note. Next: complete LedgerBridge's volume template (turn 17); the supplier said they would send it (turn 36). Fill received volumes from current AP usage and mark issued volumes as estimates (turn 18). Ask for written pricing before the commercial call (turns 32–34). Known terms: setup from EUR 2,600, supported from EUR 6,500 (turn 31); two licence models (turn 29). Scope note: the US non-payroll reporting need is outside the supplier's core scope (turn 7). Timing: Q4 target, but "not an immovable deadline" (turn 15).
suggested_routes.owner: Supplier A sends the template (turn 36); the SpendNest owner for completing it is not stated

evidence.quote: We want to understand whether LedgerBridge can give us compliant invoicing coverage across our operating markets.
That is a reporting requirement rather than our standard invoicing flow.
evidence.supports: US reporting use case is out of core scope.

evidence.quote: We would start with Singapore and Australia, then India.
I would not describe the quarter as an immovable deadline.
I will send a volume template
We should not present those two columns as equally certain.
The basic setup begins at EUR 2,600; a more supported implementation starts at EUR 6,500
Written pricing helps us follow that process internally.

concise_output: An internal supplier evaluation, not a sales conversation. SpendNest's partnerships and product team assessed LedgerBridge for e-invoicing (issuing and receiving) to support a planned receivables module. The supplier will send a volume template; SpendNest wants written pricing.
what_established: Target markets (SG, AU, then IN); a soft Q4 target; both issuing and receiving are supported; setup pricing tiers; two licence models; the template is coming from the supplier.
what_not_established: A decision to buy, approved budget, or quantified customer demand ("those conversations are still developing", turn 16). This is not SpendNest revenue and must not appear as pipeline.
next_action: Complete the volume template, keeping certain and estimated volumes separate; request written pricing.
uncertainty: Commercial numbers are verbal; per-customer cost depends on volumes not yet supplied.
